component.name: PkgDeck
component.summary: All your package managers in one app

description.p: Search, install, update, and clean up software from every package manager on your computer. PkgDeck works with APT, Flatpak, Snap, Homebrew, developer tools, container images, and firmware updates, and includes the pkd command-line tool.
Automatic updates no longer fail while a Flatpak or Snap release waits.

ul.li: With Wait for new releases on, automatic updates update the other system Flatpaks one by one instead of failing
While a Snap release waits, the other Snap updates wait for you instead of failing
A snap held with snap refresh --hold no longer shows an update that Update all never makes
A Flatpak masked with flatpak mask, or an extension of one, no longer shows an update that Update all never makes
An Alpine package pinned in /etc/apk/world, or a package DNF 4 versionlock holds back, no longer shows an update either
An Alpine package from a tagged repository, like scanelf@edge, shows its update
When one Homebrew cask changed since you reviewed it, the other casks in the run still update
Updates that failed because of the password prompt, the system helper or PkgDeck running as root are tried again
An Alpine update that stopped because a repository couldn't be reached is tried again
Updates that an older PkgDeck marked as failed are tried again
Automatic updates skip an update only after it failed twice, so a run without network doesn't hold it back
One update the helper can't run no longer stops the rest of the run
Updates that run as you still run when the system helper can't start
Activity no longer keeps what a package manager printed when a change failed, and older entries drop it too

description.p: User and System no longer swap places between screens.

ul.li: A long homepage link wraps inside the app page instead of running past its edge
PkgDeck no longer asks the desktop for its animation setting every 5 seconds: it reads it once and waits to hear about changes
Every choice between User and System shows User first, on an app's page and in its dialogs
A closing dialog keeps what it showed until it's gone, instead of going blank

description.p: Closing the password prompt no longer looks like the package manager broke.

ul.li: Closing the password prompt, or entering a wrong password too many times, says PkgDeck didn't get administrator access and nothing was changed, for every system change and not only APT

description.p: Wait before installing brand new releases, and choose System or User for any Flatpak.

ul.li: Wait for new releases, off by default, holds back versions published too recently, for the time you pick
Updates still waiting show a clock instead of a checkbox, and only Update now on their own row installs them
Search lets you choose System or User even when only one has the app's repository: installing in the other adds it, and the review says so
An app installed in one place and offered in the other stays one row in Search, with the switch
The page of an opened Flatpak file or link has a System and User switch, and the next one starts with your last choice
.flatpak files can install for the whole system, not only for you
A .flatpak file whose app is already installed offers Update, Reinstall or Downgrade beside Launch, also when it's installed for the system
Replacing an installed copy from a file says so when it finishes, and no longer offers an Undo that would remove the app

description.p: Updating several Homebrew casks asks for your password once.

ul.li: Homebrew casks you check together update in one go, so you enter your password once, and each row still says how its cask went
If you cancel while they update, PkgDeck waits for all of them to finish
A cask Homebrew skips without an error, such as a disabled one, no longer reads as updated
While a batch runs, a row only gets a green check once it's known to have worked

description.p: Updates stay right on opening, Mac apps show their icons, and Cua, Cua Driver and Cua Spaces get updates.

ul.li: Cua and Cua Driver show up with real update checks, and updating them refreshes their skills in your agents
Electron AppImages such as Cua Spaces check their own update list instead of always showing as up to date
Automatic updates of Cua Driver wait until it's idle, since updating it stops the MCP servers of open agents
pkd upgrade with a name says nothing needs doing when it's already up to date
Updates no longer lists updates that disappear a moment after PkgDeck opens
Updating PkgDeck shows one notification instead of two
Homebrew casks on a Mac show their own app icons in Installed and Updates
A cask Homebrew no longer has a definition for doesn't hide the others
Cancelling Homebrew's password dialog stops it asking again during that update, and a dialog left unanswered closes after 5 minutes
Homebrew no longer waits minutes on a server address that never answers, and PkgDeck says when it can't reach Homebrew's server

description.p: See and clean the data apps keep in your home folder.

ul.li: Clean lists the folders removed Flatpaks and snaps left in your home, unchecked
An installed Flatpak's or snap's page shows how much data it keeps, with Open data folder and Move data to Trash
App data goes to the Trash, so it can be restored
pkd info shows an app's data folder and size

description.p: Updates shows only real updates again.

ul.li: Opening Updates while Installed refreshed no longer lists every installed package as an update
Clicking a row's button while a list reloads no longer closes PkgDeck

description.p: Clean finds much more to free up, and the time sliders take exact values.

ul.li: Old snap revisions, system logs older than a week, crash dumps and crash reports can be cleaned, with your password
Unused Android system images, broken emulators and Rust toolchains no project pins show in Clean
Hugging Face models nobody read in a while, the pip cache and thumbnails show in Clean
Old Rust build output in the cache folder counts as an old project
Steam games that left their files behind show as leftovers, unchecked
Container images that lost their tag to a newer pull are found and deleted
Check every and Old after take a typed value in minutes, hours, days or weeks
Old after can be as short as a few hours
Container caches from older recipes no longer pile up

description.p: Activity opens smoothly with its list ready.

ul.li: The Activity panel slides in and out smoothly and stays inside the window frame
Activity loads after the window first appears, so its list is ready when opened
Long Activity lists and review details scroll with less work per frame
Background replies appear promptly while the app is idle
Reading Activity on macOS avoids unnecessary history writes
Changes left waiting when PkgDeck closed are settled when Activity is read

description.p: Skipped cleanups read as skipped everywhere, and Activity keeps their names.

ul.li: pkd marks a cleanup a build uses as skipped, not failed, and exits with 0
Activity names a cleaned task after it's gone, and after a restart
A task waiting for a build says since when it waits

description.p: Cleaning and automatic updates stop calling things failed when nothing went wrong.

ul.li: A cleanup task that a build uses waits for that build, then cleans on its own
Only builds that use a cache or project hold it, so the rest clean right away
A task whose files are already gone counts as cleaned
Activity keeps why each change failed, waits or was skipped
Automatic cleaning shows in Activity
Apps, container images and coding assistants update during builds
Settings names the updates that wait for builds

description.p: Links in the window open again, and automatic updates and cleaning stop getting stuck.

ul.li: GitHub in Settings, About opens the project page
A package's homepage opens in the browser
Show in folder opens an AppImage's folder in the file manager
Automatic cleaning runs once a day even when every check finds updates
Updating Cargo, Bun, pnpm, pip, uv or Composer tools updates only the outdated ones, and one failing doesn't stop the rest
A Cargo tool installed from Git is no longer reinstalled from crates.io, where its name can be another crate
Cargo tools keep the features they were built with

description.p: Installing a new version of an AppImage replaces the old one, instead of adding a second app.

ul.li: The new version keeps the old one's launch settings and where it updates from
The review says which copy it replaces, also for AppImages opened from a link
Clean offers the older copies left by earlier versions of PkgDeck

description.p: A change whose plan moved on opens for review again, instead of failing.

ul.li: An install or removal that would now do something else reopens its review, like full updates already did
Podman and Docker cleanups that changed say so the same way as other cleanup tasks

description.p: One cleanup task that changed no longer stops the others.

ul.li: If a task changed since you reviewed it, only that task is skipped and the rest are cleaned
Podman and Docker cleanups still run when an image, volume or container came into use, and keep what is in use
Automatic updates skip only the sources that can't run on their own, not the whole batch
Select all no longer checks cleanups that start unchecked, such as unused volumes and sccache
npm and pnpm installed with fnm, Volta or nvm are found again
Homebrew cleanup still runs when a file it lists changed size
Errors read more clearly, and Activity shows each reason once

description.p: Updates from different sources run at the same time, and pacman updates work on Arch again.

ul.li: APT, Flatpak, Snap and other sources update side by side, with one password per batch
The progress card names every update that is running
Selected pacman updates run in one transaction, with the packages that need their exact version
The window opens at the size you left it, maximized if it was
Screen readers read out the progress card
zypper and DNF no longer show as failed when their first check after a change is slow

description.p: Flatpak update checks no longer fail on apps from bundles or local builds.

ul.li: Apps installed from a .flatpak bundle or a local build are left out of update checks
A source that fails more than once shows once, with every reason
An opened AppImage file can launch without installing it

description.p: The AppImage works on more Linux systems, and Flatpak apps opened from a link can start.

ul.li: The AppImage and Snap start on Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13 and other systems with glibc 2.39 or newer
A Flatpak link's page shows the app as installed after installing it for the whole system
Installed Flatpak apps opened from a link or file have Launch
Flatpak links remember whether you last installed for yourself or the whole system

description.p: Choose what automatic updates wait for.

ul.li: Automatic updates and cleaning can run on battery
Automatic updates can run on a metered connection
Automatic cleaning no longer waits for a metered connection

description.p: Better pages for opened Flatpak links.

ul.li: A Flatpak link shows the app's icon, description and screenshots when its repository is set up
A Flatpak link for an app installed for all users offers Update or Reinstall instead of Install
A Flatpak link shows the version it installs instead of its branch
App descriptions keep their paragraphs and show list items one per line
Every section and running change words what it's doing the same way
The tray icon can show always, only with updates, or never
Checks can notify, install updates, or do nothing with them
Automatic updates install only from the sources you pick, and wait on metered connections

description.p: Fixes for opened files, Homebrew Casks and KDE.

ul.li: An opened file for something already installed offers Update, or for Flatpak, Reinstall or Downgrade, instead of Install
Going to another page leaves an opened file's page
Flatpak links open in PkgDeck on KDE
Homebrew Casks searches no longer fail on casks with no version for this system
Header buttons drop their labels before covering the page title
